## Important setup notes

1. Feature flag + cache: get_flag() caches for 60s. Tests that change FeatureFlag values
   must call cache.clear() after the DB change to prevent cache from serving stale values.
   Import: from django.core.cache import cache

2. FeatureFlag override pattern:
   To set PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=False in a test:
       from a_core.models import FeatureFlag
       FeatureFlag.objects.filter(key="PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED").update(enabled=False)
       cache.clear()
   Restore after test using teardown or a fixture with yield.

3. Age gate cookie: use client.cookies["age_gate"] = "ok" to pre-set the cookie,
   OR use client.get("/age-check/") then POST to set it properly.

4. Googlebot UA: pass HTTP_USER_AGENT="Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)"

5. Rate limit tests: django-ratelimit uses Django cache backend. Use
   django.test.override_settings with CACHES = {"default": {"BACKEND": "django.core.cache.backends.locmem.LocMemCache"}}
   and cache.clear() between tests to ensure rate limit counters reset.

6. Auto-hide test: needs 3 different approved users to create flags (or create flags
   directly via Flag.objects.create() with reporter set to different users).

title: [Flags] Report + takedown + auto-hide + background tasks
description:
Design doc: /workspace/docs/plans/2026-04-17-phase-0.5-public-legal-design.md Sections: "DSA — takedown + contact", "GDPR — organizer-opt-out", "Flag/report endpoint", "Auto-hide rule", "Daily flag digest email", "Nightly recompute_aggregates task" ## Goal Implement the full flagging and moderation infrastructure: - Flag/report button on event + organizer pages (authenticated users, rate-limited) - Auto-hide evaluation on each authenticated flag creation (synchronous, in view) - /takedown form (anonymous, no auth, rate-limited 5/IP/hour, saves Flag + async email) - /organizer-opt-out form (Telegram user ID verification or manual fallback) - Daily flag digest email task (django-q2 scheduled) - Nightly recompute_aggregates task (django-q2 scheduled) - All public querysets updated to use .visible() manager ## Codebase state (verified) - /workspace/reviews/views.py: has submit_review from bead 5 (MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY defined) - /workspace/reviews/urls.py: created in bead 5 with only "submit/" pattern - /workspace/ingestion/models.py: ApprovedSender model exists with telegram_user_id field - /workspace/ingestion/tasks.py: exists (read before adding to it) - /workspace/ingestion/management/commands/schedule_heartbeat.py: exists - /workspace/events/views.py: uses Event.objects.filter(status="published") — switch to .visible() - /workspace/organizers/views.py: uses Organizer.objects.get_object_or_404(...) — switch to .visible() - django-ratelimit is NOT in /workspace/pyproject.toml — must add it - /workspace/templates/cotton/footer.html: updated in bead 4 (uses hardcoded /takedown/) ## Depends on - Bead kb-a4t.1 (Flag model, aggregate fields, .visible() managers, EmailFailure) - Bead kb-a4t.2 (routing — /takedown in ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES) - Bead kb-a4t.3 (slug migration — drawer/attend URLs) - Bead kb-a4t.5 (reviews/urls.py and reviews/views.py established) ## Files to create - /workspace/templates/reviews/_flag_button.html - /workspace/templates/reviews/takedown.html - /workspace/templates/reviews/organizer_opt_out.html - /workspace/reviews/tasks.py - /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py ## Files to modify - /workspace/reviews/views.py (add flag_target, takedown_view, organizer_opt_out_view) - /workspace/reviews/urls.py (add flag, takedown, organizer-opt-out patterns) - /workspace/events/views.py (switch querysets to .visible()) - /workspace/organizers/views.py (switch querysets to .visible()) - /workspace/a_core/urls.py (add takedown and organizer-opt-out at root level) - /workspace/pyproject.toml (add django-ratelimit dependency) ## Step 1: Add django-ratelimit to /workspace/pyproject.toml In the dependencies list under [project], add: "django-ratelimit>=4.1", Then run: uv lock (or uv add django-ratelimit) to update the lockfile. ## Step 2: Add flag_target view to /workspace/reviews/views.py Add after submit_review. New imports needed at top of file: from django.http import HttpResponse from reviews.models import Flag # add Flag to existing reviews import AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD = 3 FLAG_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER = 10 # flags per day per user @require_POST @login_required @approved_required def flag_target(request): """Create a Flag. Authenticated users only. Rate limit: 10/day per user.""" from a_core.models import get_flag if not get_flag("FLAGS_ENABLED", default=True): return HttpResponse("Flagging is temporarily disabled.", status=503) from django.utils import timezone today_start = timezone.now().replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) daily_count = Flag.objects.filter(reporter=request.user, created_at__gte=today_start).count() if daily_count >= FLAG_RATE_LIMIT_PER_USER: return render(request, "reviews/_flag_button.html", {"error": "Daily flag limit reached."}, status=429) target_type = request.POST.get("target_type") target_id = request.POST.get("target_id") reason = request.POST.get("reason", "other") if target_type == "event": event = get_object_or_404(Event, pk=target_id) Flag.objects.create(reporter=request.user, event=event, reason=reason) auth_flag_count = Flag.objects.filter(event=event, reporter__isnull=False).count() if auth_flag_count >= AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD: Event.objects.filter(pk=event.pk).update(hidden=True) elif target_type == "organizer": organizer = get_object_or_404(Organizer, pk=target_id) Flag.objects.create(reporter=request.user, organizer=organizer, reason=reason) auth_flag_count = Flag.objects.filter(organizer=organizer, reporter__isnull=False).count() if auth_flag_count >= AUTO_HIDE_FLAG_THRESHOLD: Organizer.objects.filter(pk=organizer.pk).update(hidden=True) else: return HttpResponse("Invalid target.", status=400) return render(request, "reviews/_flag_button.html", {"flagged": True}) ## Step 3: Add takedown_view to /workspace/reviews/views.py IMPORTANT: The takedown form collects an event_url. The view MUST resolve this URL to a DB entity (Event or Organizer) and set the appropriate target FK on the Flag. The CheckConstraint (flag_targets_exactly_one) requires exactly one of organizer/event/review to be set — all-null target FKs are NOT allowed. URL resolution logic: - Parse the URL path using django.urls.resolve() against the project URL conf - If it resolves to event-detail: extract org_slug + event_slug, look up Event - If it resolves to organizer-profile: extract slug, look up Organizer - If resolution fails: show form error with fallback to email contact from ratelimit.decorators import ratelimit from django.urls import resolve, Resolver404 @ratelimit(key="ip", rate="5/h", method="POST", block=True) def takedown_view(request): """Anonymous DSA takedown form. No authentication required. Resolves submitted URL to a DB entity for the Flag target FK.""" if request.method == "POST": event_url = request.POST.get("event_url", "").strip() reason = request.POST.get("reason", "other") body = request.POST.get("body", "").strip() contact_email = request.POST.get("contact_email", "").strip() if not event_url and not body: return render(request, "reviews/takedown.html", {"error": "Please describe what you are reporting."}) # Resolve URL to DB entity target_event = None target_organizer = None if event_url: try: from urllib.parse import urlparse path = urlparse(event_url).path match = resolve(path) if match.url_name == "event-detail": target_event = Event.objects.filter( organizer__slug=match.kwargs["org_slug"], slug=match.kwargs["event_slug"], ).first() elif match.url_name == "organizer-profile": target_organizer = Organizer.objects.filter( slug=match.kwargs["slug"], ).first() except (Resolver404, KeyError): pass if not target_event and not target_organizer: # Could not resolve — show error with email fallback if event_url: return render(request, "reviews/takedown.html", { "error": "We could not identify the content at that URL. " "Please check the URL or contact us directly at the email below.", "values": {"event_url": event_url, "reason": reason, "body": body, "contact_email": contact_email}, }) # Body-only submission without URL — also needs a target return render(request, "reviews/takedown.html", { "error": "Please provide the URL of the content you are reporting.", }) Flag.objects.create( reporter=None, event=target_event, organizer=target_organizer, reason=reason, body=f"URL: {event_url}\n\n{body}" if body else f"URL: {event_url}", contact_email=contact_email, ) from django_q.tasks import async_task async_task( "reviews.tasks.send_takedown_notification", event_url=event_url, reason=reason, body=body, contact_email=contact_email, ) return render(request, "reviews/takedown.html", {"submitted": True}) return render(request, "reviews/takedown.html", {}) NOTE: The CheckConstraint (flag_targets_exactly_one) is NOT relaxed. Anonymous takedown flags have reporter=null but MUST target exactly one entity (resolved from URL). If the URL cannot be resolved, the form shows an error — DSA compliance email fallback. ## Step 4: Add organizer_opt_out_view to /workspace/reviews/views.py def organizer_opt_out_view(request): """GDPR opt-out form. Verified via telegram_user_id match.""" from ingestion.models import ApprovedSender if request.method == "POST": telegram_user_id = request.POST.get("telegram_user_id", "").strip() organizer_slug = request.POST.get("organizer_slug", "").strip() try: ApprovedSender.objects.get(telegram_user_id=telegram_user_id) organizer = Organizer.objects.get(slug=organizer_slug) organizer.status = "suspended" organizer.save(update_fields=["status"]) return render(request, "reviews/organizer_opt_out.html", {"submitted": True}) except (ApprovedSender.DoesNotExist, Organizer.DoesNotExist): return render(request, "reviews/organizer_opt_out.html", { "error": "Verification failed. Please contact us via the takedown form." }) return render(request, "reviews/organizer_opt_out.html", {}) ## Step 5: Create /workspace/reviews/tasks.py from django.conf import settings from django.core.mail import send_mail from a_core.models import EmailFailure def send_takedown_notification(event_url, reason, body, contact_email): """Async task: send email notification for takedown submission.""" subject = f"[Takedown] {reason}: {event_url[:100]}" message = f"URL: {event_url}\nReason: {reason}\nBody: {body}\nContact: {contact_email}" try: send_mail( subject=subject, message=message, from_email=settings.DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL, recipient_list=[settings.DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL], fail_silently=False, ) except Exception as exc: EmailFailure.objects.create( recipient=settings.DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL, subject=subject, body_preview=message[:500], error_message=str(exc), ) ## Step 6: Create /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py from django.conf import settings from django.core.mail import send_mail from django.db.models import Avg, Count from a_core.models import EmailFailure def daily_flag_digest(): """Daily django-q2 task: send summary of unresolved flags to admin.""" from reviews.models import Flag unresolved = Flag.objects.filter(resolved=False).order_by("created_at") count = unresolved.count() if count == 0: return lines = [f"Unresolved flags: {count}\n"] for flag in unresolved[:50]: target = flag.organizer or flag.event or flag.review or "(anonymous takedown)" lines.append(f"- [{flag.reason}] {target} (reporter: {flag.reporter})") body = "\n".join(lines) try: send_mail( subject=f"[Kinky Bubbles] Daily flag digest — {count} unresolved", message=body, from_email=settings.DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL, recipient_list=[settings.DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL], fail_silently=False, ) except Exception as exc: EmailFailure.objects.create( subject="Daily flag digest", body_preview=body[:500], error_message=str(exc), ) def recompute_aggregates(): """Nightly django-q2 task: recompute denormalized aggregate fields (F8). Recomputes: Organizer.follower_count, Organizer.avg_rating, Organizer.rating_count, Event.attendance_count, Event.interested_count, Event.rating_count. Does NOT update hidden (synchronous in flag view). POST params: target_type, target_id, rating, body.""" from a_core.models import get_flag if not get_flag("RATINGS_ENABLED", default=True): return render(request, "reviews/_rating_form.html", {"error": "Ratings are temporarily disabled."}, status=503) target_type = request.POST.get("target_type") target_id = request.POST.get("target_id") try: rating = int(request.POST.get("rating", 0)) except (ValueError, TypeError): rating = 0 if not 1 <= rating <= 5: return render(request, "reviews/_rating_form.html", {"error": "Rating must be between 1 and 5."}, status=400) body = request.POST.get("body", "").strip() with transaction.atomic(): if target_type == "organizer": organizer = get_object_or_404(Organizer, pk=target_id, status="approved") review, created = Review.objects.update_or_create( author=request.user, organizer=organizer, defaults={"rating": rating, "body": body, "event": None}, ) agg = Review.objects.filter(organizer=organizer).aggregate( count=Count("pk"), avg=Avg("rating") ) Organizer.objects.filter(pk=organizer.pk).update( rating_count=agg["count"] or 0, avg_rating=agg["avg"], ) organizer.refresh_from_db() return render(request, "reviews/_organizer_rating_display.html", { "organizer": organizer, "rating_count": organizer.rating_count, "avg_rating": organizer.avg_rating, "user_rating": str(rating), "MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY": MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY, }) elif target_type == "event": event = get_object_or_404(Event, pk=target_id, status="published") review, created = Review.objects.update_or_create( author=request.user, event=event, defaults={"rating": rating, "body": body, "organizer": None}, ) count = Review.objects.filter(event=event).count() Event.objects.filter(pk=event.pk).update(rating_count=count) return render(request, "reviews/_rating_form.html", { "submitted": True, "target_type": "event", "target_id": str(event.pk), }) else: return render(request, "reviews/_rating_form.html", {"error": "Invalid target type."}, status=400) ## reviews/urls.py — create new file from django.urls import path from . import views urlpatterns = [ path("submit/", views.submit_review, name="review-submit"), ] NOTE: Bead 6 will expand this file with flag and takedown patterns. The 'flag-target' pattern is added in bead 6; do not add it here. ## a_core/urls.py — add reviews include Add this line to urlpatterns in /workspace/a_core/urls.py: path("reviews/", include("reviews.urls")), Add import at top: from django.urls import include (already present — verify) ## Organizer profile context — /workspace/organizers/views.py In organizer_profile view, after the following/going_venue_ids block, add: from reviews.views import MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY rating_count = organizer.rating_count avg_rating = organizer.avg_rating show_rating = rating_count >= MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY user_review = None if request.user.is_authenticated: try: user_review = organizer.reviews.get(author=request.user) except Exception: user_review = None Then add to the context dict: "rating_count": rating_count, "avg_rating": avg_rating, "show_rating": show_rating, "user_review": user_review, "MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY": MIN_RATINGS_FOR_DISPLAY, NOTE: organizer.rating_count requires the aggregate fields added in bead 1. organizer.reviews is the related_name defined on Review.organizer FK. ## Organizer profile template — /workspace/templates/organizers/profile.html READ THE FILE FIRST before editing. description:
Design doc: /workspace/docs/plans/2026-04-17-phase-0.5-public-legal-design.md
Section: "Hardening — Switch drawer endpoint from PK-based to slug-based"

## Goal
Replace integer-PK-based drawer and attend URLs with org_slug/event_slug-based URLs.
Remove event_id from GeoJSON payload. Update map.js to use slugs and composite selection key.
Update store.js to use string composite key. Update integration tests.

## Codebase state (verified)
- /workspace/events/urls.py: has path("<int:event_id>/drawer/") and path("<int:event_id>/attend/")
- /workspace/events/views.py:
    event_drawer(request, event_id) — lookup by pk=event_id

    selectEvent(eventId) dispatching CustomEvent with detail: { eventId: eventId }

- /workspace/events/views.py
- /workspace/static/js/events/map.js
- /workspace/static/js/events/store.js

Replace the two PK patterns with slug patterns. event_detail already uses slug pattern.

    urlpatterns = [

Update event_drawer (currently at line 164):

Remove event_id from GeoJSON feature properties in event_list.

    feature["properties"].update(
        {
            "event_id": event.pk,
            "event_slug": event.slug,

Remove the "event_id": event.pk line. The remaining properties (event_slug, org_slug, title) stay.

## 3. map.js click handler — /workspace/static/js/events/map.js

Replace the map click handler (currently at lines 102-111):

Old:
    map.on('click', 'event-markers', function (e) {
      var feature = e.features[0]

    window.addEventListener('events:selection-changed', function (e) {

        ['==',

        '#a855f7',

description:
Design doc: /workspace/docs/plans/2026-04-17-phase-0.5-public-legal-design.md Sections: "Scope — two-tier prefix redesign", "AgeGate (JuSchG)", "Hardening — X-Robots / robots.txt / OG tags" ## Goal Restructure LoginWallMiddleware to two-tier public prefix design, add AgeGateMiddleware, make X-Robots-Tag conditional, replace static robots.txt with a dynamic view, and add a conditional OG meta tag block in _base.html. ## Codebase state (verified) - /workspace/accounts/middleware.py — LoginWallMiddleware reads getattr(settings, "LOGIN_WALL_ENABLED") and sets X-Robots-Tag on EVERY response. Has PUBLIC_PREFIXES = ("/accounts/", "/healthz", "/robots.txt"). - /workspace/a_core/urls.py — robots.txt served via TemplateView; no age-check URL present. - /workspace/pages/views.py — three views (home_view, test_partial_view, test_skeleton_hx). No robots or age views. - /workspace/templates/_base.html — has extra_head block but no og_meta block inside head. - /workspace/templates/layouts/_default.html — extends _base.html, uses c-footer cotton component. - No /workspace/templates/age_check.html exists yet. ## Files to modify - /workspace/accounts/middleware.py (full rewrite) - /workspace/a_core/urls.py (replace static robots.txt view, add age-check URL) - /workspace/a_core/settings.py (add AgeGateMiddleware to MIDDLEWARE, remove now-redundant env var reads) - /workspace/templates/_base.html (add og_meta block) - /workspace/pages/views.py (add age_check_view and robots_txt_view) ## Files to create - /workspace/templates/age_check.html ## Depends on Bead kb-a4t.1 — needs get_flag() from a_core.models ## LoginWallMiddleware rewrite — /workspace/accounts/middleware.py Replace the entire file. Key changes from current code: - Remove getattr(settings, "LOGIN_WALL_ENABLED") — replaced by get_flag() - Split PUBLIC_PREFIXES into ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES and PUBLIC_READ_PREFIXES - X-Robots-Tag only set when NOT in public-read mode (not on every response) """Accounts middleware for kinky-bubbles.""" import urllib.parse from django.shortcuts import redirect from django.template.response import TemplateResponse from a_core.models import get_flag _ROBOTS_TAG = "noindex, nofollow, noarchive" ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES = ( "/accounts/", "/healthz", "/robots.txt", "/impressum", "/privacy", "/terms", "/takedown", "/age-check", ) PUBLIC_READ_PREFIXES = ("/events", "/o/", "/") class LoginWallMiddleware: def __init__(self, get_response): self.get_response = get_response def __call__(self, request): path = request.path public_read = get_flag("PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED", default=True) always_public = any(path.startswith(p) for p in ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES) read_public = public_read and any(path.startswith(p) for p in PUBLIC_READ_PREFIXES) if always_public or read_public: response = self.get_response(request) if not (always_public and read_public) and not read_public: response["X-Robots-Tag"] = _ROBOTS_TAG return response # Auth enforcement if not request.user.is_authenticated: next_url = urllib.parse.quote(request.get_full_path(), safe="/") response = redirect(f"/accounts/login/?next={next_url}") response["X-Robots-Tag"] = _ROBOTS_TAG return response if not (request.user.is_staff or request.user.is_approved): response = TemplateResponse( request, "errors/403_pending_approval.html", status=403, ) response.render() response["X-Robots-Tag"] = _ROBOTS_TAG return response response = self.get_response(request) response["X-Robots-Tag"] = _ROBOTS_TAG return response IMPORTANT — X-Robots-Tag logic clarification: - Routes in ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES that are NOT also in PUBLIC_READ_PREFIXES (e.g. /impressum, /accounts/) should still receive X-Robots-Tag when PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=False (rollback). - Routes in PUBLIC_READ_PREFIXES when PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True: NO X-Robots-Tag (indexed). - Routes in PUBLIC_READ_PREFIXES when PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=False: they fall through to auth enforcement, which sets the tag. - Admin and other authenticated-only routes: X-Robots-Tag always set. Simplified correct logic: if read_public: # Public read mode — no X-Robots-Tag on public content return self.get_response(request) if always_public: response = self.get_response(request) response["X-Robots-Tag"] = _ROBOTS_TAG return response # Auth-required path... [auth checks, each setting X-Robots-Tag before returning] ## AgeGateMiddleware — add to /workspace/accounts/middleware.py Add after LoginWallMiddleware class: class AgeGateMiddleware: """JuSchG age gate: redirect to /age-check/ on first HTML request without cookie. Only active when PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True (bypass entirely in closed-beta). Exempt: ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES routes. Bot user-agents bypass so SEO crawling is not blocked. Only triggers on text/html responses (not API/JSON/static). """ BOT_AGENTS = ("googlebot", "bingbot", "slurp", "duckduckbot", "baiduspider", "yandexbot") def __init__(self, get_response): self.get_response = get_response def __call__(self, request): if not get_flag("PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED", default=True): return self.get_response(request) if any(request.path.startswith(p) for p in ALWAYS_PUBLIC_PREFIXES): return self.get_response(request) ua = request.META.get("HTTP_USER_AGENT", "").lower() if any(bot in ua for bot in self.BOT_AGENTS): return self.get_response(request) if request.COOKIES.get("age_gate") == "ok": return self.get_response(request) # Only gate text/html requests (not XHR/JSON/static assets) accept = request.META.get("HTTP_ACCEPT", "") if "text/html" in accept: return redirect("/age-check/") return self.get_response(request) NOTE on Accept header: Only redirect when "text/html" is explicitly in the Accept header. This avoids false positives on API/HTMX requests (which send "application/json" or "*/*"). Browser page loads always send "text/html" in Accept. HTMX requests typically include "text/html" too, but that is acceptable — unauthenticated HTMX requests to public routes with no age cookie should also be gated. ## MIDDLEWARE order in /workspace/a_core/settings.py The current MIDDLEWARE list has "accounts.middleware.LoginWallMiddleware" at index 8. Add AgeGateMiddleware immediately AFTER LoginWallMiddleware: "accounts.middleware.LoginWallMiddleware", "accounts.middleware.AgeGateMiddleware", # NEW — add this line Also remove the now-redundant env var definitions from settings.py (LoginWallMiddleware no longer reads them; context_processors was updated in bead 1): Remove: LOGIN_WALL_ENABLED = env.bool("LOGIN_WALL_ENABLED", default=True) Remove: MAP_ENABLED = env.bool("MAP_ENABLED", default=True) Remove: INVITES_ENABLED = env.bool("INVITES_ENABLED", default=True) ## Age-check view + robots.txt view — add to /workspace/pages/views.py Add these imports at the top of the file (if not already present): from django.shortcuts import redirect # add to existing import from django.views.decorators.http import require_http_methods Add these functions after existing views: @require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"]) def age_check_view(request): if request.method == "POST" and request.POST.get("confirm") == "yes": next_url = request.POST.get("next", "/") if not next_url.startswith("/"): next_url = "/" response = redirect(next_url) max_age = 365 * 24 * 3600 if request.POST.get("remember") else None response.set_cookie("age_gate", "ok", max_age=max_age, httponly=True, samesite="Lax") return response next_url = request.GET.get("next", "/") return render(request, "age_check.html", {"next_url": next_url}) def robots_txt_view(request): from a_core.models import get_flag from django.http import HttpResponse public = get_flag("PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED", default=True) if public: content = "User-agent: *\nAllow: /\n\nUser-agent: *\nDisallow: /admin/\n" else: content = "User-agent: *\nDisallow: /\n" return HttpResponse(content, content_type="text/plain") NOTE: The current pages/views.py already imports render and HttpResponse — verify before adding. ## URL wiring — /workspace/a_core/urls.py Current file imports TemplateView and uses it for robots.txt. Make these changes: 1. Add import: from pages.views import age_check_view, robots_txt_view 2. Remove the TemplateView robots.txt entry (currently at lines 17-23) 3. Add two new paths: path("robots.txt", robots_txt_view, name="robots-txt"), path("age-check/", age_check_view, name="age-check"), 4. Remove the TemplateView import if it is no longer used elsewhere in the file. ## Age-check template — create /workspace/templates/age_check.html NOTE: This template extends _base.html directly (not layouts/_default.html) since it must render without the navbar/footer structure (minimal legal gate page). Requirements: WCAG AA accessible, keyboard-navigable, German + English copy, remember-me checkbox, Leave button to google.de. {% extends "_base.html" %} {% load i18n %} {% block title %}{% trans "Age Verification" %} — Kinky Bubbles{% endblock title %} {% block layout %}

{% trans "Age Verification / Altersverifizierung" %}

{% endblock layout %} ## OG meta block — /workspace/templates/_base.html Inside the , add after the existing {% block extra_head %} block: {% if PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED %} {% block og_meta %}{% endblock og_meta %} {% endif %} This wrapper ensures OG tags are suppressed when PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=False (rollback). Individual page templates fill the og_meta block in a later phase. ## Verification steps 1. python manage.py check 2. python manage.py test accounts pages 3. Functional checks (use Django test client or curl against running dev server): a. GET /events/ anon, PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True, no age_gate cookie -> 302 to /age-check/ b. GET /events/ anon, PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True, cookie age_gate=ok -> 200 c. GET /events/ anon, PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=False -> 302 to /accounts/login/ (NOT /age-check/) d. GET /impressum/ anon, no cookie -> 200 (ALWAYS_PUBLIC, no age gate) e. GET /robots.txt with PUBLIC_READ_ENABLED=True -> body contains "Allow: /" f.     from django.conf import settings
    from django.core.cache import cache
    from django.db import models

    class FeatureFlag(models.Model):

        enabled = models.BooleanField(default=True)
        description = models.TextField(blank=True)
        updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)
        updated_by = models.ForeignKey(
            settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL
        )
        def __str__(self):
            return f"{self.key}={self.enabled}"
        class Meta:
            verbose_name = "feature flag"
            verbose_name_plural = "feature flags"

    class EmailFailure(models.Model):
        recipient = models.EmailField(blank=True)
        subject = models.CharField(max_length=300, blank=True)
        body_preview = models.TextField(blank=True)
        error_message = models.TextField()
        created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
        resolved = models.BooleanField(default=False)
        class Meta:
            verbose_name = "email failure"
            verbose_name_plural = "email failures"
            ordering = ["-created_at"]

    def get_flag(key: str, default: bool = False) -> bool:
        """Single read path for all feature flag checks. Cached 60s."""
        cache_key = f"feature_flag:{key}"
        val = cache.get(cache_key)
        if val is None:
            try:
                val = FeatureFlag.objects.get(key=key).enabled
            except FeatureFlag.DoesNotExist:
                val = default
            cache.set(cache_key, val, timeout=60)
        return val

The existing NoSignupAdapter has only is_open_for_signup. Add two overrides:

1. Replace is_open_for_signup(self, request) entirely:
  from django.conf import settings
  from django.utils import timezone

  def is_open_for_signup(self, request):
      if not getattr(settings, 'INVITES_ENABLED', True):
          return False
      code = request.GET.get('code') or request.session.get('invite_code')
      if not code:
          return False
      from accounts.models import InviteCode
      try:
          invite = InviteCode.objects.get(code=code, redeemed_by__isnull=True)
      except InviteCode.DoesNotExist:
          return False
      if invite.expires_at and invite.expires_at <= timezone.now():
          return False
      request.session['invite_code'] = code
      return True

2. Add save_user override. Signature: save_user(self, request, user, form, commit=True).
The code redemption must be atomic to handle a race where two requests redeem the same code simultaneously.
Strategy: call super() first (saves the user), then atomically mark the code redeemed via a filtered UPDATE.
If updated == 0, the code was already taken — delete the newly-created user and raise ValidationError.

Note on error path: allauth calls save_user inside its signup view's form.save() path. Raising django.forms.ValidationError from save_user is NOT caught by allauth's form validation layer — it will propagate as an unhandled 500 error unless the signup view has a try/except. To handle this gracefully, re-raise as a django.core.exceptions.ValidationError (not django.forms.ValidationError) so Django's middleware can convert it, OR add a top-level try/except in the view. The safe approach for 0.4 scale: log the race condition and return the user object without redemption (the invite code stays unredeemed but no 500 occurs). A staff member can manually clean up. If strict rejection is required, use django.forms.ValidationError and add a test for the 500-vs-400 behaviour. For now, use the lenient approach:

  from django.db import transaction
  import logging
  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

  def save_user(self, request, user, form, commit=True):
      user = super().save_user(request, user, form, commit=commit)
      if commit:
          code = request.session.get('invite_code')
          if code:
              from django.utils import timezone as tz
              from accounts.models import InviteCode
              with transaction.atomic():
                  updated = InviteCode.objects.filter(
                      code=code, redeemed_by__isnull=True
                  ).update(redeemed_by=user, redeemed_at=tz.now())
                  if updated == 0:
                      # Race: code already redeemed. Log and continue (lenient).
                      # The new user account is created but invite code is not marked.
                      # Staff can reconcile. At 0.4 scale (5-15 users) this is acceptable.
                      logger.warning(
                          'Invite code %s already redeemed when saving user %s',
                          code, user.pk
                      )
              request.session.pop('invite_code', None)
      return user

            feature = venue_to_geojson(venue)
            self.assertEqual(feature['geometry']['type'], 'Point')

            self.assertEqual(feature['properties']['privacy'], 'public')

            feature = venue_to_geojson(venue)

```python
"""Accounts middleware for kinky-bubbles."""
from django.conf import settings
from django.http import HttpResponseForbidden
from django.shortcuts import redirect


class LoginWallMiddleware:
    """Hard login-wall for Phase 0.3 (staff-only).

    Anonymous users: redirect to /accounts/login/?next=<path>.
    Authenticated non-staff: 403 (will relax to is_approved at 0.4).
    Adds X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive to every response.
    Kill-switch: LOGIN_WALL_ENABLED=False in settings bypasses the wall.
    """

    PUBLIC_PATHS = {"/accounts/login/", "/accounts/logout/", "/healthz", "/robots.txt"}

    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):
        if not getattr(settings, "LOGIN_WALL_ENABLED", True):
            response = self.get_response(request)
            response["X-Robots-Tag"] = "noindex, nofollow, noarchive"
            return response
        if request.path not in self.PUBLIC_PATHS and not request.user.is_authenticated:
            return redirect(f"/accounts/login/?next={request.path}")
        if request.user.is_authenticated and not request.user.is_staff:
            return HttpResponseForbidden("Not available yet.")
        response = self.get_response(request)
        response["X-Robots-Tag"] = "noindex, nofollow, noarchive"
        return response
```

title: C. django-q2 heartbeat task + 5-minute schedule
description:
Wire a real heartbeat task into django-q2 that proves the worker loop is alive. This is the go/no-go gate for phase 0.2.

Design doc: docs/plans/2026-04-17-phase-0.1-schema-admin-design.md, section: django-q2 heartbeat, Test plan.

## Context
settings.py already has Q_CLUSTER configured with orm='default'. ingestion/models.py (from bead B) has HeartbeatLog(ran_at, note). This bead adds the task function and the Schedule entry.

## What to do

### 1. ingestion/tasks.py
Create this file:

import logfire
from django.utils import timezone
from .models import HeartbeatLog

def heartbeat():
    """Inserted every 5 minutes by django-q2 scheduler. Proves worker loop is alive."""
    log = HeartbeatLog.objects.create(note='scheduled heartbeat')
    logfire.info('heartbeat ok', heartbeat_log_id=log.pk, ran_at=log.ran_at.isoformat())

### 2. Schedule via django-q2 Schedule model
In a data migration or a management command — the cleanest approach for 0.1 is a management command that seeds the schedule (idempotent, safe to re-run):

Create ingestion/management/__init__.py, ingestion/management/commands/__init__.py, ingestion/management/commands/seed_q_schedule.py:

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
from django_q.models import Schedule

class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = 'Seed django-q2 schedule entries (idempotent)'

    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        Schedule.objects.update_or_create(
            name='heartbeat',
            defaults=dict(
                func='ingestion.tasks.heartbeat',
                schedule_type=Schedule.MINUTES,
                minutes=5,
                repeats=-1,  # repeat forever
            ),
        )
        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS('Schedule seeded: heartbeat every 5 minutes'))

### 3. Logfire dependency
logfire>=3.0 is already in pyproject.toml dependencies — no uv add needed. Import pattern in tasks.py is: import logfire (no config needed here; Logfire reads LOGFIRE_TOKEN env var at startup).

### 4. Verify locally (manual smoke test)
- Run: python manage.py seed_q_schedule
- Run qcluster in background: python manage.py qcluster &
- IMPORTANT: Wait at least 5 minutes (the schedule interval) before checking — HeartbeatLog rows do NOT appear immediately on qcluster startup, only after the first schedule interval fires.
- After 5+ minutes: python manage.py shell -c 'from ingestion.models import HeartbeatLog; print(HeartbeatLog.objects.count())'

- Shortcut (no wait needed): call heartbeat() directly:

3. Manual smoke test (requires running DB and qcluster):
   python manage.py qcluster &
   (Wait at least 5 minutes — the schedule is every 5 minutes, not every 10 seconds)
   python manage.py shell -c "from ingestion.models import HeartbeatLog; print(HeartbeatLog.objects.count())"
   Expected: >= 1

4. Shortcut smoke — call task directly without qcluster:

title: B. Domain schemas + admin: organizers, venues, events, ingestion, reviews
description:
Create all six domain apps with their models, migrations, and admin customizations. All model definitions are verbatim from the design doc. Design doc: docs/plans/2026-04-17-phase-0.1-schema-admin-design.md, sections: Data model, Admin customizations. ## Apps to create (all via python manage.py startapp ) - organizers/ - venues/ - events/ - ingestion/ - reviews/ Add all five to INSTALLED_APPS in a_core/settings.py (after 'accounts'). ## FK convention (critical) All FKs to the user model use the STRING 'settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL' resolved at runtime — never import the User class directly in models.py. Pattern: from django.conf import settings author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE, ...) Cross-app FKs use string app_label.ModelName notation: raw_message = models.ForeignKey('ingestion.RawMessage', null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL) ## Models (exact field definitions in design doc — reproduce exactly) ### organizers/models.py — Organizer Fields: name, slug (unique), description, avatar (ImageField upload_to='organizers/'), website (URLField), telegram_channel. Trust tier: status (choices: candidate/approved/suspended, default=candidate), verified_badge (BooleanField default=False), approved_at (DateTimeField null/blank), approved_by (FK to settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL null/blank SET_NULL). GDPR consent (F5): consent_recorded_at (DateTimeField null/blank), consent_method (CharField choices: telegram_forward_implied / explicit_opt_in / verified_public_source, blank=True), consent_notes (TextField blank=True). Timestamps: created_at (auto_now_add), updated_at (auto_now). ### venues/models.py — Venue Fields: name, slug (unique), address (max_length=300 blank), neighborhood (max_length=100 blank). Geo (F4): latitude, longitude as DecimalField(max_digits=9, decimal_places=6, null=True, blank=True). Privacy: privacy_mode (choices: public / neighborhood_blur / private address on request, default=public), blur_radius_m (IntegerField default=250). Other: url (URLField blank), notes (TextField blank), created_at (auto_now_add). ### events/models.py — Tag Fields: slug (SlugField unique), label (max_length=100), kind (CharField choices: theme/format/identity/bubble), description (TextField blank). ### events/models.py — Event Fields: title (max_length=300), slug (SlugField max_length=200 — NOT globally unique, unique per organizer via constraint), description (TextField blank), organizer (FK Organizer PROTECT related_name=events), venue (FK Venue PROTECT null/blank related_name=events), tags (M2M Tag blank related_name=events). Time: start (DateTimeField), end (DateTimeField null/blank). Price: price_min_cents (IntegerField null/blank), price_max_cents (IntegerField null/blank), currency (max_length=3 default=EUR), is_free (BooleanField default=False), sliding_scale (BooleanField default=False). External: external_url (URLField blank), tickets_url (URLField blank). Lifecycle status (choices: draft/review/published/cancelled/rejected/archived, default=draft), published_at (DateTimeField null/blank). Provenance (F7): raw_message = FK('ingestion.RawMessage', null=True, blank=True, on_delete=SET_NULL). Timestamps: created_at (auto_now_add), updated_at (auto_now). class Meta: indexes = [Index(fields=['status','start']), Index(fields=['organizer','start'])] constraints = [ UniqueConstraint(fields=['organizer','slug'], name='event_slug_unique_per_organizer'), UniqueConstraint(fields=['organizer','start','title'], name='event_dup_guard_org_start_title'), ] ### events/models.py — EventImage Fields: event (FK Event CASCADE related_name=images), image (ImageField upload_to=events/), alt (max_length=300 blank), is_cover (BooleanField default=False), order (IntegerField default=0). ### ingestion/models.py — RawMessage Fields: source_type (CharField choices: telegram_bot_forward / telegram_telethon / email_submission / web_form), sender_id (max_length=100 blank), channel_id (max_length=100 blank), message_id (max_length=100 blank), received_at (auto_now_add), raw_payload (JSONField), text (TextField blank), enriched_payload (JSONField default=dict blank), extraction_status (CharField choices: pending/extracted/failed/skipped, default=pending), extraction_error (TextField blank). ### ingestion/models.py — SourceFailure Fields: source_type (max_length=50), raw_message (FK RawMessage null/blank SET_NULL), stage (max_length=50), error_class (max_length=200), error_message (TextField), occurred_at (auto_now_add), resolved (BooleanField default=False). ### ingestion/models.py — HeartbeatLog Fields: ran_at (auto_now_add), note (max_length=200 blank). ### reviews/models.py — Review Fields: author (FK settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL CASCADE related_name=reviews), organizer (FK Organizer null/blank CASCADE related_name=reviews), event (FK Event null/blank CASCADE related_name=reviews), rating (IntegerField validators=[MinValueValidator(1), MaxValueValidator(5)]), body (TextField blank), created_at (auto_now_add). class Meta: constraints = [ CheckConstraint( check=Q(organizer__isnull=False) ^ Q(event__isnull=False), name='review_targets_exactly_one', ), ] ## Migrations Run: python manage.py makemigrations organizers venues events ingestion reviews Run: python manage.py migrate All must succeed clean. ## Admin customizations (admin.py in each app) ### organizers/admin.py — OrganizerAdmin @admin.register(Organizer) class OrganizerAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin): list_display = ['name', 'status', 'verified_badge', 'event_count'] list_filter = ['status', 'verified_badge'] search_fields = ['name', 'slug', 'telegram_channel'] readonly_fields = ['created_at', 'updated_at', 'approved_at'] actions = ['mark_approved_record_consent'] def event_count(self, obj): return obj.events.count() event_count.short_description = 'Events' @admin.action(description='Mark approved + record consent') def mark_approved_record_consent(self, request, queryset): from django.utils import timezone queryset.update( status='approved', approved_at=timezone.now(), approved_by=request.user, consent_recorded_at=timezone.now(), consent_method='explicit_opt_in', ) ### events/admin.py — EventAdmin + EventImageInline class EventImageInline(admin.TabularInline): model = EventImage extra = 0 @admin.register(Event) class EventAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin): list_display = ['title', 'organizer', 'start', 'status'] list_filter = ['status', 'start', 'tags', 'organizer'] search_fields = ['title', 'description'] inlines = [EventImageInline] readonly_fields = ['created_at', 'updated_at', 'published_at', 'raw_message_preview'] actions = ['publish_events', 'reject_events', 'archive_events'] def raw_message_preview(self, obj): if not obj.raw_message: return '—' from django.utils.html import format_html return format_html('
{}
', obj.raw_message.text or str(obj.raw_message.raw_payload)) raw_message_preview.short_description = 'Raw message' @admin.action(description='Publish selected events') def publish_events(self, request, queryset): from django.utils import timezone queryset.update(status='published', published_at=timezone.now()) @admin.action(description='Reject selected events') def reject_events(self, request, queryset): queryset.update(status='rejected') @admin.action(description='Archive selected events') def archive_events(self, request, queryset): queryset.update(status='archived') ### ingestion/admin.py — RawMessageAdmin @admin.register(RawMessage) class RawMessageAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin): list_display = ['source_type', 'received_at', 'extraction_status', 'text_preview'] list_filter = ['extraction_status'] readonly_fields = [f.name for f in RawMessage._meta.get_fields() if hasattr(f, 'name')] # all read-only in 0.1 def text_preview(self, obj): return obj.text[:80] if obj.text else '(no text)' text_preview.short_description = 'Text preview' ### reviews/admin.py — ReviewAdmin @admin.register(Review) class ReviewAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin): list_display = ['author', 'target_display', 'rating', 'created_at'] def target_display(self, obj): if obj.organizer: return f'Organizer: {obj.organizer}' if obj.event: return f'Event: {obj.event}' return '(none)' target_display.short_description = 'Target' Also register Venue, Tag, EventImage with basic admin.register decorators. ## Done when - [ ] All 5 apps exist with models.py and admin.py - [ ] python manage.py makemigrations --check exits 0 (nothing unmigrated) - [ ] python manage.py migrate runs clean - [ ] All UniqueConstraints and CheckConstraint exist in migrations - [ ] python manage.py createsuperuser works and /admin/ loads all registered models - [ ] Organizer bulk action 'Mark approved + record consent' appears in admin - [ ] Event bulk actions publish/reject/archive appear in admin - [ ] RawMessageAdmin fields are all read-only in 0.1
notes:
VERIFICATION COMMANDS (run after all steps complete):

1. No unmigrated models:
   python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run
   Expected: 'No changes detected' and exit 0.

2. Migrations apply cleanly:
   python manage.py migrate
   Expected: exit 0, all migrations applied.

3. Admin loads all registered models (requires superuser):
   python manage.py createsuperuser --username admin --email admin@example.com --noinput (set DJANGO_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD=testpass123)
   Then run: python manage.py runserver and visit http://localhost:8000/admin/ — confirm organizer, venue, event, tag, eventimage, rawmessage, sourcefailure, review, heartbeatlog all appear.

4. Smoke-test each app's models import cleanly:
   python -c "from organizers.models import Organizer; from venues.models import Venue; from events.models import Event, Tag, EventImage; from ingestion.models import RawMessage, SourceFailure, HeartbeatLog; from reviews.models import Review; print('all imports ok')"
   Expected: 'all imports ok'

5. UniqueConstraints in migrations:
   python -c "from django.db import connection; cursor = connection.cursor(); cursor.execute(\"SELECT conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname IN ('event_slug_unique_per_organizer','event_dup_guard_org_start_title','review_targets_exactly_one');\"); print([r[0] for r in cursor.fetchall()])"
   Expected: list of 3 constraint names.

NOTE ON PER-APP TESTS: There are no per-app test directories in this project. All integration tests are in tests/test_phase_0_1.py (bead F). The done-when criterion 'pytest per-app smoke green' refers to the tests in bead F passing — run 'pytest tests/test_phase_0_1.py' after bead F is complete.

RAWMESSAGEADMIN READONLY FIX: Do NOT use the description's pattern (hasattr(f, 'name')). Use the NOTES-corrected pattern: readonly_fields = [f.name for f in RawMessage._meta.get_fields() if hasattr(f, 'column')] — this excludes reverse relations that have no column attribute and avoids AttributeError.

title: A. Foundation: custom User + AUTH_USER_MODEL + i18n wiring + vector extension
description:
Set up the foundational pieces that all other phase 0.1 beads depend on. Must be completed and migrated BEFORE any other app migration runs.

CRITICAL ORDER TRAP: AUTH_USER_MODEL must be set in settings.py before ANY migration runs. If migrations have already run with the default auth.User, switching is painful (Django trap). On a fresh repo/DB this is safe; verify no existing migrations in other apps before starting.

## Files to touch
- a_core/settings.py (AUTH_USER_MODEL, INSTALLED_APPS, MIDDLEWARE, i18n block)
- accounts/models.py (create)
- accounts/admin.py (create)
- accounts/migrations/0001_vector_extension.py (create by hand)
- accounts/migrations/0002_user.py (auto-generated, must depend on 0001)
- locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/ (create directory)

## Step 1: Create accounts app
Run from repo root (/Users/jonat/code/personal/kinky-bubbles):
  python manage.py startapp accounts

## Step 2: accounts/models.py
```python
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser
from django.db import models


class User(AbstractUser):
    is_approved = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    approved_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    approved_by = models.ForeignKey(
        'self',
        null=True,
        blank=True,
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        related_name='approved_users',
    )
```

## Step 3: a_core/settings.py changes

### 3a. AUTH_USER_MODEL (add near top of file, before INSTALLED_APPS)
```python
AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'accounts.User'
```

### 3b. INSTALLED_APPS: add 'accounts' before 'pages'
```python
    # local
    'a_core',
    'accounts',
    'pages',
```

### 3c. MIDDLEWARE: add LocaleMiddleware immediately after SessionMiddleware (before CommonMiddleware)
Current order: SecurityMiddleware → WhiteNoise → SessionMiddleware → CommonMiddleware
Add: 'django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware' between SessionMiddleware and CommonMiddleware.
Result:
```python
    'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware',
    'django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware',
    'django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware',
```

### 3d. i18n settings block (add after USE_I18N = True line)
```python
LANGUAGES = [('en', 'English'), ('de', 'Deutsch')]
LOCALE_PATHS = [BASE_DIR / 'locale']
```
Note: USE_I18N, LANGUAGE_CODE, TIME_ZONE already set — do NOT duplicate them.

## Step 4: accounts/admin.py
```python
from django.contrib import admin
from django.contrib.auth.admin import UserAdmin

from .models import User


@admin.register(User)
class CustomUserAdmin(UserAdmin):
    fieldsets = UserAdmin.fieldsets + (
        ('Approval', {'fields': ('is_approved', 'approved_at', 'approved_by')}),
    )
    list_display = ['username', 'email', 'is_approved', 'is_staff']
```

## Step 5: Create locale directory
  mkdir -p locale/de/LC_MESSAGES

## Step 6: pgvector migration (HAND-WRITTEN — create before running makemigrations)
Create accounts/migrations/0001_vector_extension.py:
```python
from django.db import migrations


class Migration(migrations.Migration):
    dependencies = []

    operations = [
        migrations.RunSQL(
            sql='CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;',
            reverse_sql=migrations.RunSQL.noop,  # do NOT drop on reverse — data-loss risk on shared DB
        ),
    ]
```

## Step 7: Generate the User model migration
Run: python manage.py makemigrations accounts
This produces accounts/migrations/0002_user.py (or similar). Open that file and verify its dependencies list includes ('accounts', '0001_vector_extension'). If it was auto-numbered as 0001, rename 0001_vector_extension.py to be explicit and edit the auto-generated file's dependencies accordingly. The vector migration MUST come first.

## Step 8: Run migrations
Compose image must be pgvector/pgvector:pg17 (check docker-compose.yml before running).
Run: python manage.py migrate
Expected: all migrations apply cleanly, including CREATE EXTENSION.

## Done when
- [ ] AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'accounts.User' in a_core/settings.py
- [ ] python manage.py migrate runs clean on a fresh DB (pgvector/pgvector:pg17 image)
- [ ] CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector migration is the FIRST accounts migration (0001_*)
- [ ] Auto-generated User migration lists 0001_vector_extension as a dependency
- [ ] LocaleMiddleware in MIDDLEWARE between SessionMiddleware and CommonMiddleware
- [ ] LANGUAGES includes 'en' and 'de'; LOCALE_PATHS = [BASE_DIR / 'locale']
- [ ] locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/ directory exists
- [ ] python manage.py makemessages -l de runs without error (empty catalog is acceptable at this stage; a non-empty catalog is required after bead F ships)
notes:
VERIFICATION COMMANDS (run after all steps complete):

1. Fresh DB migration check:
   python manage.py migrate
   Expected: all migrations apply cleanly, no errors.

2. pgvector extension installed:
   psql $DATABASE_URL -c "SELECT * FROM pg_extension WHERE extname='vector';"
   Expected: one row returned.

3. AUTH_USER_MODEL correct:
   python -c "from django.conf import settings; assert settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL == 'accounts.User', settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL"
   Expected: no output (assertion passes).

4. LocaleMiddleware present:
   python -c "from django.conf import settings; assert 'django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware' in settings.MIDDLEWARE, settings.MIDDLEWARE"
   Expected: no output (assertion passes).

5. i18n settings correct:
   python -c "from django.conf import settings; codes = [c for c,_ in settings.LANGUAGES]; assert 'en' in codes and 'de' in codes, codes"
   Expected: no output (assertion passes).

6. makemessages runs without error (non-empty catalog not required until bead D CI step goes green, but the command must exit 0):
   python manage.py makemessages -l de
   Expected: exit 0. An empty catalog is acceptable here — the CI enforcement of non-empty content is added in bead D and requires at least one {% trans %} tag in templates.

MIGRATION ORDER INVARIANT: Run 'python manage.py showmigrations accounts' and confirm 0001_vector_extension appears before 0002_user (or whatever Django auto-numbers the User migration). If they came out in wrong order, rename files and fix the dependencies list in the auto-generated file.
